scout.purpose: Coroutine tests need one controlled scheduler so delays, child jobs, dispatcher changes, and cancellation become fast and deterministic.
scout.realWorldUse: ViewModels, repositories, retry loops, timeouts, debouncing, and concurrent operations otherwise produce slow or flaky tests.
scout.outcome: Use runTest, share TestCoroutineScheduler, choose Standard or Unconfined test dispatchers, and assert intermediate scheduling deliberately.

sections.title: runTest owns test scope and virtual time

blocks.text: runTest creates a TestScope, skips delays under virtual time, waits for structured children, and reports uncaught coroutine failures. StandardTestDispatcher queues new work until the test yields or advances the scheduler, providing control over intermediate states. UnconfinedTestDispatcher starts new coroutines eagerly until their first suspension, making simple state tests concise but execution order less production-like. Neither makes uncontrolled real dispatchers deterministic.

blocks.caption: One shared scheduler controls dispatcher execution and the retry boundary.

sections.title: All test dispatchers must share one scheduler

blocks.text: Inject dispatchers or CoroutineContext into code that switches execution. TestDispatchers used by one test must share runTest.testScheduler; otherwise advancing one clock does not run work scheduled on another. Local JVM tests replace Dispatchers.Main where ViewModel code depends on it, with cleanup after each test. Avoid creating new TestCoroutineScheduler instances in dependencies. Fakes should support suspension and cancellation instead of returning everything synchronously.

blocks.caption: One shared scheduler controls dispatcher execution and the retry boundary.

blocks.title: One test, one scheduler
blocks.text: Every injected TestDispatcher should use runTest.testScheduler.

sections.title: Advance only when the contract requires it

blocks.text: Use runCurrent to execute tasks scheduled at current virtual time, advanceTimeBy to move a specified duration, and advanceUntilIdle to drain available work. Prefer state or result assertions over checking scheduler internals. For debounce and retry, assert before and after exact boundaries. Verify cancelled jobs do not publish later and failed children surface to the test. Some multithreaded race properties require dedicated stress or integration tests beyond a single virtual scheduler.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

blocks.title: Do not hide real dispatchers in code under test
blocks.text: A real IO or Default dispatcher escapes virtual time and reintroduces races.

inspect.title: Unify two test clocks
inspect.code:
val io = StandardTestDispatcher()
val cpu = StandardTestDispatcher()
val repo = Repo(io, cpu)
walkthrough: Each dispatcher creates its own scheduler by default.
Advancing the runTest scheduler may not execute either dependency queue.
Construct both with the testScheduler supplied by runTest.
inspect.expectedOutput: One advance operation deterministically controls all repository coroutine work.

trap_check.why: Intermediate loading, debounce, or cancellation behaviour becomes unobservable.
trap_check.fix: Advance only to the exact state boundary being tested.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Write deterministic tests for a repository with loading state, exponential retry delays, operation timeout, child cancellation, and dispatcher switching.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Every TestDispatcher shares one scheduler. Intermediate states are asserted before completion. Cancelled work never publishes a late result.

recall.answer: Queues new work until the scheduler runs it.

recall.prompt: What must injected test dispatchers share?
